parsed.rationale: Both `MainActorNotificationMessageSequence` (line 129 of `MainActorMessage.swift`) and `AsyncNotificationMessageSequence` (line 103 of `AsyncMessage.swift`) are `type-alias-object` declarations in the same `Core` package. Although the structural pipeline reports `shared_field_count: 3` and flags them as exact duplicates, type aliases by definition carry no stored fields of their own — the shared count reflects the shape of their underlying aliased types, not duplicated logic. The two aliases almost certainly resolve to different concrete generic specialisations (one pinned to `@MainActor`, the other a plain async sequence), making the structural similarity intentional and domain-meaningful rather than accidental redundancy. Collapsing them would erase a semantically important actor-isolation distinction that the separate file names (`MainActorMessage.swift` vs `AsyncMessage.swift`) already signal.
